reading:
The track series is the owner's lens's favourite. The feedback lens scored it 8.6 to 9.1 across rounds 9 to 13 and called it "the Signal Box line language the owner asked for", "high style". Soul liked two things: the lamp legend (#6dff9c only for now and live) and, from round 11, the lit run of track from the NOW lamp (Relit 8.2).

What every lens liked: lines that carry order. That means the Coming up fortnight from a lit NOW lamp, To do's timetable margin with amber lamps, the Chat hung from Vera's screen to a lit ring at the box, the setup track, and Status's Who-answers chain. Also liked: the ring-and-bracket head (interaction: "the best head idea on the panel"), green-black slate with steel-cyan, and the chat's date given once with the times beside it.

What sank it was never the lines that carry order. Three kinds of fault did.
(1) Boxes and small faults, listed round after round by system, type, interaction, usability and skeptic:
- Ideas as a card grid with warm kind tints that read brown and plum (6 cards above the fold).
- Status as plates inside plates, and Settings as today's cards.
- Selects in boxed forms, and Ideas' tab and Kind select doing the same job.
- An icon-only right side of the bar.
- The To do page with no "was due" words, so late showed by colour alone.
- "Here" as a faint cell with a 5px dot.
- One target under 44px on every page.
- Thick rounded pewter monitor cases and an olive-bronze setup tray.
- Tiny margin dates, and stamps that wrapped.
By round 13 the system lens called it "the page from two rounds ago".
(2) Light. At screenGlow 0.8 on #74f0a3 its halos were thinner than today's. Relit (7.52) fixed that. Aglow then showed that a relight confined to lit things differs by only 0.1-0.9% of pixels and reads as a near-duplicate.
(3) Where Signal Lines drew lines without order (a ring on every head, buffer stops that read as pins, round ticks that looked like stops, a form inside the bracket), the lines read as a git graph or a subway map.

What would make it win: keep every line that carries order and the lit NOW lamp, and change the page at scale where the lineage was weakest. Those places are Ideas, Status, Settings, the To do page, the family's side of Chat, and the month. The changes are:
- one-line rows with tabular facts;
- late said in amber words;
- words for every place in the bar and a "here" that survives the squint;
- 0 small targets;
- thin cased tubes;
- the tube's real two-layer halo on the short live list, and an afterglow that shows in a still.
Every change must show at half size, not only in the lamps. The dice mutant (t1-track-mut) already relights, so the refinement, the revival and the graft must each carry structure. The greeting's title has never been varied in this lineage, so the three briefs propose three: "What's the plan?", "What shall we line up?" and "What's next for us?".

briefs.name: Track Diagram, Trued
briefs.hypothesis: Track Diagram lost its rounds on boxes and small faults, never on its lines, and the owner's lens always ranked it at or near the top. Keep every line that carries order and the lit NOW lamp, and fix every fault the judges cited, most-cited first. Home drops to three lines, every box becomes a one-line listing row, the To do page says late in words, the bar names every place, 'here' is a latched key, and the tube's halo comes back on the live list. That should lift the lenses that held it at 6.0-7.1 (system, type, skeptic, usability) while keeping feedback and soul. Page-scale change is guaranteed: Ideas, Status, Settings and To do change drawing, not only colour.

SYSTEM RULES, carried on every page
1. Light on the live list only (feedback r10/r11/r13, soul r10/r11/r13, skeptic r11). Use phosphor_kit.md's drawings at full strength:
- the mark and its blinking cursor (E2);
- 'mind' and the new key word under the two-layer E1 halo;
- Send and every page's one primary with E3's ring and pool;
- Home's box with E4's resting halo, and a field while it is typed in;
- the E5 focus ring;
- the monitors (E12-E17: VT323 with three halos and a 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen, falloff, the 80px spill, the power lamp);
- her screens (E19);
- the greeting's green pool from below at the original's 0.13 alpha, with its scanlines inside the mask (E7; soul r13 asked for this);
- the top haze at the original's strength (E6).
Lamps are E20 glowing dots (4px, 10px at 65%, 18px 1px at 48%). Only Coming up's NOW lamp breathes: one breathing lamp per view (soul r11).
The lit run of track keeps Aglow's drawing: #6dff9c with a 1px white-hot --hot core held for 65%, then fading into the steel. It runs from NOW to the next stop on Coming up, into the lit NOW tick on To do, and between on-lamps on Status's chain. Add soul r13's 'travelling wake': a brighter 12px segment slides along the run from the lamp to the next stop every 4s (background-position animation). It stays static under reduced motion, and a still shows the lit run.
2. Visible row afterglow (soul r10/r11, feedback r13; an open problem for five rounds). Every listing row (Home To do, Lately added, the kids, Ideas, To do page, Status, Settings) gets, on :hover and :focus-within:
- a 12% steel wash, color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 12%, transparent);
- a 2px inset #86d9a6 left edge;
- its stop lamp, where it has one, lit in its own colour.
The light comes on in var(--glow-in) 0.12s and fades over var(--afterglow) 1.2s. Check it in motion-glow-1..3.png.
3. Type: the lineage's own written scale from Track Diagram, Large Setting (r11-mut-1), which feedback r11 and type r11 asked to breed in. As tokens:
- --t-label 13px: DM Mono 500 for stamps; DM Sans 600 for labels in sentence case; tracked caps (+.05em at most) for eyebrows and column heads only.
- --t-small 15px: controls, facts and kind words. Kind words rise from 13 to 15 (type r11), so no label sits below the text beside it.
- --t-body 17px, line-height 1.6.
- --t-head 24px: Archivo 600 at wdth 80.
- --t-title 48px on desktop and 34px below 40rem, so no title wraps on the phone or on Sign in (Large Setting's fault).
A thing's name is the body in 600, never a size of its own. Every figure in a column or stamp is DM Mono tabular with its slashed zero; counts inside sentences stay DM Sans, so zero is drawn one way per role (type r10). Use text-wrap: pretty on titles and balance on ledes.
4. Square for the family, round for the machine (style r12/r13: 'rounded cards feel stock'). Plates, rows, fields, keys and bubbles-them take a 3px radius. The greeting, tubes, her bubbles and lamps keep their rounds.
5. Thin cases (feedback r11/r13, lessons open problem). Every .crt gets:
- a 3px graphite bezel (linear-gradient #2e3439 to #23292d);
- an outer radius of 14px and glass of 11px;
- a hairline lip (inset 0 0 0 1px #060908, inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .07));
- a 12px chin with eight vent ticks (repeating-linear-gradient 2px on / 3px off at #3b4247) and E12's power lamp;

6. Words for every place in the bar (feedback r12, interaction r11-r13, usability r11-r13). Copy base.html (as H/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/base.html did) so Memory, Family, Status and Settings show icon plus word.
'Here' is a latched steel key (interaction r10, skeptic r7/r9): a tinted solid #26313a, ink #ebe6da, the icon in steel. Its 2px #9fc2da cap sits exactly on the bar's bottom rule, so the cap reads as the occupied section of the track, with a 7px steel lamp centred on the cap (the parent's dot, now inside a strong cell). On the phone tab bar, the same cell with the cap on top.
7. 0 targets under 44px, and sentence case on every control and link. Links are underlined steel.

HOME (1280)
- Greeting: as the parent (speaker row, the box under its new title, the ways to start at 44px with an 8px gap, the Next up tube at the right), with the E7 pool and no corner wash.
- 'Finish setting up': on the slate tray with the #644e29 amber edge and no olive fill (skeptic r10-r13; Aglow did it). Keep the across track. The first undone step's ring is lit #6dff9c with the lamp halo, 'you are here' (soul r11). The others are amber hollow rings, and each link is a 44px row.
- Coming up: keep the fortnight line exactly (feedback: 'keep every track exactly as drawn').
  - Plate titles drop to 17/600 so the 34px DM Mono day numerals lead, with OCT/THU stacked at 13px (type r10).
  - 'in 2 days' is one line, nowrap.
  - The NOW lamp gets the word 'now' in 13px DM Mono lit phosphor above it (interaction r7: a lamp's meaning must not rest on a legend).

- To do: the timetable margin widens to 8.5rem, with one-line stamps (type r7/r13): '2 days ago' and 'yesterday' in amber beside filled amber lamps, then Relit's steady lit NOW tick with 'now', then 'in 2 days · 19:56'. Rows are one line on the tray with no plate boxes: a square tick well (1.15rem, with a 44px hit area pulled back by negative margins), the title, and WHO at the right, with a hairline between rows. The head reads 'To do', then '2 late' as an amber link to /tasks?status=open, then 'All 4 →'.
- Lately added loses its rail, which caps Home at three lines (system r10). It becomes one-line rows: kind ring lamp (a 1.6rem ring in the kind colour, icon inside, no plate tint), title, kind word (15px in the kind colour), 'for Maya, Theo' in dim, and '#1' in DM Mono at the right. No kind fills anywhere (feedback r10/r11/r13, skeptic r11/r12).

CHAT (keep the track from her screen down the left gutter to the lit ring at the box)

What’s the *plan*? (in variants//templates/_ask.html, copied from /home/user/FamilyDB/src/familydb/web/templates/_ask.html:

). The lineage has so far only carried 'What’s on your mind?', so this is its first proposal. FamilyDB is the family's planner, and 'What's the plan?' is the family's own kitchen-table phrase for it. It invites them to tell Vera the weekend, the reminder or the idea to keep, rather than a stray thought. The glowing word is the job itself, as the lamp on the track is the plan itself. At 16 characters it holds one line on a phone even at the 34px title step.

briefs.name: Signal Box Relaid
briefs.hypothesis: The owner's strongest signal across the whole tournament has been Signal Box's complete line language (feedback 8.6-9.1). It lost the other lenses to decoration, not to the language itself: a ring on every head, curved drops read as a subway map or git graph, buffer stops read as pins, round ticks looked like stops, a 5px 'here' dot, and a whole form inside the To do bracket. Relay it with a railway's own drawing: straight runs, 45° turnouts, proper T buffer stops, lines only for time, sequence or belonging, square ticks, 44px targets, a strong 'here', and the tube's halo on what is live. That should keep feedback and soul at the top and win back interaction, whose 'best head idea on the panel' was the bracket, and the skeptic.
briefs.brief:
H = /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness.

START
- Copy H/tour/t1-a/palettes/r10-idea-3.json and H/tour/t1-a/variants/r10-idea-3/ to the new id.
- Read the first line language in H/tour/donors/variants/r7-idea-2/templates/ (Signal Box: _ui.html page_head L37-59 and ring L62, login.html, 404.html) with its css in H/tour/donors/palettes/r7-idea-2.json. Read Signal Lines' version in H/tour/donors/variants/r9-idea-4/src/lines.css and templates/ (ideas.html, tasks.html, status.html, setup.html, chat.html).
- Take the light from H/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-mut-4/src/phosphor.css and relight.css.
- Appended css, 60,000 characters: replace the parent's .rail/.page-head::before masthead and curved elbows rather than adding beside them.

TOKENS: the parent's, except:
- screen #6dff9c; glow, screenGlow and topGlow 1.0; washGlow 0;
- --rail #607385 (2px running line) and --wire #394652 (1px brackets and branch ticks);
- steel #a7c4d8 for 'here' and rings;
- --buffer #8a9aa8.
Slate trays #0f1519 behind every board that carries a line.

THE GRAMMAR (one rule set, written as tokens and a few shared classes: .rail, .stop, .terminus, .turnout, .buffer, .bracket)
- A line is drawn only where there is an order: time (Coming up, To do, Chat, the plans list), sequence (setup, the fallback chain, Sign in's steps), or belonging (a head's bracket gathering its own controls). Sets with no order (Lately added, the kids, Keys, Connected to, Settings, Ideas) keep their lamps and get no rail.
- A line runs straight. Every turn is a 45° chamfer, never a curve or a rounded elbow. A signal box's NX panel draws no curves; git graphs and subway maps do. Draw the chamfer as a 14px square pseudo-element: background: linear-gradient(135deg, transparent calc(50% - 1px), var(--rail) 0 calc(50% + 1px), transparent 0).
- A line begins at a terminus ring: 2.6rem on a page head, 1.5px in the section's ink, dark glass #0f1519 inside, no halo.
- A line that ends with nothing after it ends at a T buffer stop drawn properly: a 14x2 bar with a 2x10 upright, in --buffer, never a dot (L239 caveat). Where a link follows, the buffer stands beside it ('All plans →').
- A stop is a 12px lamp in one legend:
  - hollow steel ring: to come;
  - filled sage #86d9a6: done;
  - filled amber with an amber stamp: late / needs a look;
  - pewter hollow ring: off;
  - red ring: only for a thing that has stopped;
  - #6dff9c with the E20 halo (4px, 10px 65%, 18px 48%): now, live, your turn.
  Print the legend once as a one-line key on Status, under its boards.
- A tick box is never a lamp. It is a square 1.15rem well beside the stop, with a 44px hit area (usability and skeptic r9).

BAR
- Words for every place (copy base.html as H/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/base.html did).
- The bar's foot is the main line: a 1px #2e343b rule across the page. Under the current place it becomes a 3px bright steel run (#a7c4d8), the width of the key, with a 12px steel ring lamp centred on it.
- The key above is latched: a tinted solid #26313a with #ebe6da ink whose foot is that run.
- So 'here' is a latched cell, a lit run and a lamp: strong in the squint, and the dot the owner liked is kept (feedback r8), no longer alone (interaction r9, skeptic r9).
- On the phone tab bar, the run is on its top edge.

PAGE HEADS (every inner page, from Signal Lines' L243 with its fixes)
- The terminus ring round the page's icon, the 48px Archivo condensed title beside it, and the lede under.
- When the head holds controls, a 1px --wire bracket drops from the ring's foot, turns one 45° chamfer and runs right under the controls row, ending in a 6px upright tick at the right edge (not a buffer, so it never reads as a pin).
- The bracket holds keys only, never a form (system and feedback r9: 500px on a phone). Folds it opens drop below the bracket.
  - Ideas: All ideas / Restaurants latched keys and a 'Save a thought for later' disclosure key. 'Add an idea' is the primary at the top right on the title's baseline, outside the bracket (every lens, r7).
  - To do: Open / Done / Cancelled / All latched keys and a Search field with its key. 'Add something to do' is the primary on the title's baseline.
  - Plans: List / Month keys, and Earlier / Later on Month.
  - Status, Settings, Vera, Family, Memory, Wishes and New idea hold nothing: the ring alone, with no drop and no line (interaction and system r9).

HOME
- Greeting: the parent's (box, ways to start at 44px with an 8px gap, the Next up tube on a thin 3px graphite case with chin, vent ticks and power lamp), with E7's pool at 0.13 and the new title.
- 'Finish setting up' becomes Signal Box's vertical station line.
  - An amber terminus ring round the warning icon, then a 2px --rail line down the left.
  - A 12px amber hollow stop per step; the first undone step's stop is lit #6dff9c with the halo ('you are here').
  - Each step is a 44px underlined sentence-case link.
  - The line ends at a T buffer beside 'All the setup steps'.
  - The tray is slate with the #644e29 amber edge and no olive fill.
- Coming up: Signal Box's fortnight.
  - An across track from the breathing NOW lamp (the page's one breathing lamp, labelled 'now' in 13px DM Mono), with the lit run and its hot core to the first stop.
  - Stops are cyan hollow rings.
  - Date designators sit above the rail (34px DM Mono numeral, OCT/THU stacked at 13px).
  - Plates hang below each stop on a 1px drop, which is Signal Box's plate: title 17/600, date line 15px, 'in 2 days' in DM Mono.
  - The rail ends at a T buffer with 'All plans →' beside it (Signal Box's own ending), never running past its last lamp.
- To do: the timetable.
  - A 9rem margin with one-line stamps: '2 days ago' and 'yesterday' in amber beside filled amber stops, a steady lit NOW tick with 'now', then 'in 2 days · 19:56'.
  - The rail on the margin's edge.
  - Rows one line: square tick well, title, WHO. No plate boxes; hairlines on the tray.
  - It ends at a T buffer beside 'All 4 →'.
- Lately added and the kids' wishes: rows with their ring lamps and no rail (kind colour in the ring only, no tints).
- Something to eat: a slate row.

CHAT (Signal Lines' L209)
- Vera's glyph screen in a terminus ring at the head, with a 2px --rail track down the left gutter.
- Her lines hang beside the track by her 28px glyph, with times in the left margin.
- Each family line:
  - a steel hollow stop on the track;
  - a 1px --wire branch tick straight across to the family's right-hand bubble;
  - their time set at the tick's end, right beside the bubble ('19:47' in DM Mono 13px), so time and bubble share one sight line (skeptic r10, interaction r11).
  - Family bubbles are square plates #1c252b with a 3px steel bar on the right edge, text left-aligned.
- The day mark is given once, as a 45° crossover tick with 'Sun 27 Sep'.
- The track ends in the lit #6dff9c ring with the lamp halo and a tick across into the box: 'your turn'.
- Below 40rem the track and ticks go, and times move into the bubble heads (interaction r9).

TO DO PAGE
- The bracket head as above.
- The timetable: a 9rem margin with one-line stamps ('Sun 27 Sep 19:56', amber when late) and stops on the rail; the lit NOW tick with 'now'.
- Each row one line: square tick well, '#4' and title, WHO, DUE in words ('was due 2 days ago' in amber, 'due in 2 days, 19:56'), and a 44px pencil Edit key opening the form under the row.
- Late and the words come from config.FAMILYDB_APP.clock.today() in the template (as H/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/tasks.html L26-37, L103-104, L137, L149).
- The rail ends at a T buffer beside '4 shown'.

IDEAS: the bracket head. One filter row (Search, Kind without 'restaurant', Status, For, Filter). One-line rows with kind ring lamps and no rail. The radar tube on a thin case at 1.0.

PLANS
- Month: bracket head; today's cell carries the NOW lamp, lit, beside a steel date key; events have cyan stops.
- List: a vertical station line. Date designators sit in the margin, stops on the rail, and each row holds title and time. The lit run goes from today's lamp to the next plan, and the line ends at a T buffer.

STATUS
- Who answers is the main line: a vertical --rail dropping from its terminus ring through Chat messages, The weekend digest and Web lookups, lit between on-lamps.
- 'If that one cannot' leaves by a 45° turnout onto a short siding that ends at a T buffer: the fallback drawn as what it is, a siding with nowhere else to go.
- Keys and Connected to: lamps, no rail. All rows one line on trays, with no plate inside.
- The spend tube on top. The lamp legend key under the boards.

SETUP PAGE (/setup, L210): steps as a numbered station line. Numbers sit in 2.2rem rings on a vertical rail: done steps filled sage with a tick, the current one lit #6dff9c with the halo, later ones hollow. Each step is a 44px row.

SETTINGS: the overview as rows on a tray, with no rail (a set). The section nav's current item is the same 'here' turned vertical: a latched cell with a 3px steel run on its left edge and a lamp.

SIGN IN and 404 (Signal Box's L239, with its caveats fixed)
- Desktop: the thin-cased tube at left (22rem), the words at right on a short vertical rail.
- Sign in: the rail runs from a steel terminus ring at the title to a lit #6dff9c stop level with the password field's centre ('waiting for you') and ends at the Sign in button.
- 404: the rail runs past 'Not found' to a proper T buffer beside 'Back to the start': the end of the line.
- Phone: the tube, then the line.

FORM (New idea): ring head with nothing to hold; the form on a raised slate box; fields as wells with E4; 'Add it' with E3.

LIGHT: the same live list as the kit (E1 'line', E2 mark, E3 the primary, E4 box, E5 focus, E12-E17 tubes, E19 her screens, E20 lamps). Nothing else glows; lines and rings stay matte steel.

TYPE: the parent's faces (Archivo condensed heads, DM Sans, DM Mono stamps) on a written scale of 13 / 15 / 16 / 24 / 44. Stamps nowrap, none under 13px. Controls sentence case. Figures tabular.

briefs.title:
What shall we *line* up? The glowing key word is 'line':

in a copied _ask.html. 'Line up' is how a family says it will arrange things: the weekend, a trip, a reminder, a present. It asks them to tell Vera what to put in order. The lit word is the motif this whole design is drawn in: the question glows at the head of the page as the NOW lamp glows at the head of the track. At 22 characters it holds one line on a phone at 30px.

briefs.name: Track Diagram, Branch Lines
briefs.hypothesis: Track Diagram's lines were praised where they drew the family's own order. The pages it left as boxes (Ideas' card grid, Status's plates, the plain month, a chat with one track) are where it lost system, type and skeptic. Four gems from lower-half designs are each already a line or a lamp that draws the page's own data. Rebuilt as branch lines of the same diagram, they give Chat, Status, Ideas and Plans a drawing of their own content. That answers the owner's 'reflect more of the page content', the r11-r12 lesson that light must carry data, and the system lens's 'page from two rounds ago', while Home keeps the fortnight line and lit NOW lamp every lens asked to keep.
briefs.brief:
H = /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness.

START
- Copy H/tour/t1-a/palettes/r10-idea-3.json and H/tour/t1-a/variants/r10-idea-3/ to the new id.
- Take the light from H/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-mut-4/src/phosphor.css and relight.css, with its .now-run spans.
- Appended css, 60,000 characters: delete the parent's card grid, kind tints, plate boxes and olive setup fill as you replace them.

TOKENS: the parent's, except:
- screen #6dff9c; glow, screenGlow and topGlow 1.0; washGlow 0;
- bezel #2a3035 (thin 3px graphite case with hairline lip, vent chin and power lamp);
- --rail #58697a, --tray #0f1519, steel #a7c4d8.
Every grafted piece is drawn in these: steel lines on slate, lamps from the lineage's legend, phosphor only on the glass and on what is live.

GRAFT 1: CHAT AS A DOUBLE-TRACK MAIN LINE (L033, two-track tape chat, Braun Signal r10, a gem)
Source: H/rounds/r10/variants/r10-wild-1/templates/_ui.html macro chat_line (from L96) and waiting_line; sheet.css .thread > li (grid 3fr 56px 2fr), .tape-time, .said-bot/.said-them > .bubble (~1380-1440), phone 1999-2003; shot H/tour/gallery/r10-wild-1/chat.png.
It replaces the parent's left-gutter track, margin times and dotted leaders: the .thread.line rules in src/track.css, and chat_line in templates/_ui.html L76-92 and chat.html.
The rebuild:
- .thread > li is grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 4.5rem minmax(0,1fr).
- The centre column carries two 2px --rail rails 8px apart: the up line and the down line. They run from Vera's glyph screen, in a steel terminus ring centred at the head, down to the box.
- Each message is a station. Vera's 28px glyph screen sits on the left rail with her bubble to its left (green-black glass #111712, a 30% brand edge, her light pooling from the corner, rounded as the machine). The family member's steel hollow ring with their initial sits on the right rail with their bubble to its right (a square #1c252b plate with a 3px steel bar on its rail side, text left-aligned).
- The time is printed between the rails at the station ('19:47' in DM Mono 13px, tabular, on a #0b0e0c patch), so side, mark and time each tell who spoke and every time sits beside its bubble.
- The date is given once as a crossing tie across both rails ('Sun 27 Sep').
- Bubbles cap at 46ch.
- At the box the two rails converge through 45° into one short run that ends in the lit #6dff9c ring with the lamp halo ('your turn').
- Below 40rem it folds to one rail down the left edge, the family's bubbles indented 1rem and the times back in the bubble heads.

GRAFT 2: STATUS'S INDICATION PANEL (L143, Status lamp strip with its tally, Single Quote r12, a gem)
Source: H/rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-4/templates/status.html L63-64; sheet.css L1531-1536 (.lamp-strip, .lamp-count, .lamp-count .figure); shot H/tour/gallery/r12-wild-4/status.png.
It goes at the top of Status beside the spend tube, and replaces the three plate columns as the first read.
The rebuild, as the signal box's block shelf:
- One recessed well: #080c0d, a 1px #20272b edge, inset 0 1px 3px #000a, square 4px radius.
- Three banks of lamps inside it, in the order of the lists below (Who answers, Keys, Connected to), divided by 1px steel uprights. Each bank has a 13px label caption under it.
- Each lamp sits in a 44px link cell to its row (add ids to status.html rows; title attribute = the row's name). This fixes the caveat that the strip's lamps had no labels and were not links. Following one lands the row with E10's flash.
- Working: #6dff9c with the E20 halo. Partly: an amber half. Off (no key, not set up): a pewter hollow ring. Red: only for something that has stopped.
- Under the well, the tally as a figure: '6 working · 7 off', in 40px Archivo 600 wdth 75 tabular, with 15px words.
Below it, the three lists become one-line rows on trays (lamp, name, detail), with no plates inside. Who answers keeps its chain rail with the lit run between on-lamps.

GRAFT 3: IDEAS' LINE FROM HOME (L063, distance dial on Ideas, Braun Signal r10, a gem)
Source: H/rounds/r10/variants/r10-wild-1/templates/ideas.html L9-48 (the drive parsing, span and marks); _ui.html dial macro L160-213 (SVG with no viewBox, marks at their share of the width); sheet.css .dial ~978-1010; shot H/tour/gallery/r10-wild-1/ideas.png.
It replaces the parent's radar tube beside the filters (templates/ideas.html .scope .on-radar; track.css .scope.has-screen, .on-radar).
The rebuild is a wide thin-cased tube under the head, about 9rem tall, drawing a railway line out of HOME:
- the HOME lamp lit #6dff9c at the left, the one live lamp;
- a phosphor running line to the right, with mileposts at 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h and 3 h on a square-root scale, so places 20 minutes out do not pile up (the source's caveat);
- each place as a station tick with its number ('7'), labels alternating above and below the line so none collide (Mapped's r13 fault), the nearest brightest;
- at the left, in VT323 under E13: 'The line from home · 10 places', 'Nearest #7 Pumpkin patch · 18 min NW', 'Furthest #4 Cannon Beach weekend · 2 h 45 min W'. The compass stays in the words.
The list under it is one-line rows keyed to the line: kind ring lamp, title and kind word, for whom, DRIVE ('18 min NW', tabular, right-aligned), and '#7'. Pointing at or focusing a row lights its station for 0.12s with a 1.2s afterglow, via one :has() rule per number (.ideas-page:has(#idea-7:is(:hover, :focus-within)) .st-7), which is soul r10's 'a stop lamp lights when its row is hovered'.
Keep 9 rows above the fold at 1280x900.

GRAFT 4: THE MONTH AS WEEK TRACKS (L145, busy days carry the pulse, Signal Catalogue r13, a gem)
Source: H/rounds/r13/variants/r13-wild-2/sheet.css table.month td:has(.event)::after and today's variant (L2113-2135), static/pulse.svg; shot H/tour/gallery/r13-wild-2/plans.png.
It replaces the parent's plain cells and green dot on Plans > Month (templates/plans_month.html, track.css table.month rules).
The rebuild, as the scout's own note for this lineage ('each busy day gets a short run of steel track, with the lit lamp only on today'):
- Each week row carries a 2px --rail along the foot of its cells, drawn by each td's ::after so it reads as one line Monday to Sunday.
- A day holding a plan puts a cyan (#70dcf4) ring lamp on its segment (two plans, two lamps), and its event plate carries the same cyan ring.
- Today puts the NOW lamp on the rail (#6dff9c, E20, breathing: the page's one breathing lamp). The run from today to the next plan day in that week is lit with Aglow's hot-cored run, fading into the steel.
- Days gone by dim their rail to #2e343b, and their lamps go hollow.
- Weekend columns sit a step lighter (color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface-3) 55%, transparent), about 2-3 dE) so outings' days read at a glance.
- No strip above the grid, so the month stays on one screen. This is the fault that sank Flight Console's flight plan (L072), which is not taken.

THE LINEAGE'S FIXES, carried too
- Home: the parent's layout, kept.
  - The fortnight line with the breathing NOW lamp, labelled 'now', and a visibly fading lit run.
  - Setup on slate with an amber edge; the next step's ring lit.
  - To do's timetable with a one-line 8.5rem margin, amber late stamps and a steady lit NOW tick.
  - Lately added as one-line rows without rail or tints (kind colour in the ring only).
  - The kids as rows.
- The light list: E1 'next', E2 mark, E3 the one primary, E4 box, E5 focus, E7 pool at 0.13, E12-E17 tubes, E19, E20.
- The bar: words for Memory, Family, Status and Settings (copy base.html as H/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/base.html). 'Here' is a backlit steel key (L186: radial #879dae to #748a9b, 22% white top edge, dark ink, no halo), with the parent's small lamp on the bar rule under it.
- The To do page:
  - Show as latched keys and one Search.
  - 'Add something to do' as the primary on the title baseline.
  - One-line rows with a square tick well, title, WHO, DUE in words ('was due 2 days ago' in amber) and an Edit key.
  - Late computed from config.FAMILYDB_APP.clock.today() as in r13-idea-1/templates/tasks.html L26-37, L103-104, L137, L149.
- Settings: rows on a tray.
- 0 small targets; sentence case everywhere.
- The row afterglow: a 12% steel wash with a 2px sage edge, in 0.12s and out over 1.2s.

briefs.title:
What’s *next* for us? The glowing word is 'next':

in a copied _ask.html. A family says this when it is deciding the weekend, the next outing or the next thing to get done, and every page of this design is drawn as what comes next down the line, from the lit NOW lamp to the next stop. It invites the family to tell Vera the next plan, reminder or idea to keep, in their own 'us'. At 20 characters it holds one line on a phone. The lit word is the diagram's own meaning of #6dff9c: now, and what comes next.
